design_note: Show replanning as a specific change to remaining work after an authoritative observation. The completed lookup stays completed, while a proposed refund becomes unnecessary; no plan step can erase external history.

source.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source.concept: Interleaving actions with observations lets a system revise its plan when external information changes the next useful step.
source.scope: Original ShopAssist plan records apply the feedback principle. They do not reproduce ReAct prompts, benchmark results or a framework implementation.

lesson.anchor: When a deterministic workflow beats an agent
lesson.title: Replan the remaining work, keep completed facts
lesson.intro: ShopAssist plans to investigate PAY-B and possibly propose its refund. An authorized lookup discovers that RF-9 already refunded the full captured balance. The plan must respond to that fact.

data.invariant: The completed lookup and confirmed receipt survive every plan revision.

read: The first plan describes conditional work, not a promise to execute.
The observation supplies an authoritative reason to change the next step.
Replanning changes the remaining proposal while preserving the completed lookup.
lesson.question: Should replanning mark the lookup pending again simply because the plan text changed?
lesson.answer: No. Its accepted observation remains available with the same provenance. The new plan skips an unnecessary refund and explains RF-9. Refresh only if the task requires newer evidence; changing an outline alone does not invalidate completed work or authorize another financial effect.
lesson.takeaway: Adapt the path to new observations without rewriting completed history.
lesson.assumption: Fictional plan states; RF-9 fully refunds PAY-B and is current. No new refund was submitted, and explanation acceptance remains task-specific.
